result.note: Tests the proposed Economic Stabilisation Fund (size, mechanism) and the unchanged FY26 fiscal deficit target; skipped the 'expected' spending direction.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the 'Economic Stabilisation Fund' proposed by the Union Finance Minister in March 2026:
items: It was proposed with a size of USD 6.20 billion.
The government raised its FY26 fiscal deficit target to accommodate the fund.
It creates a pre-authorised pool of cash that can be deployed quickly when supply chains snap or energy prices spike.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the government is sticking to its FY26 fiscal deficit target of INR 15.58 trillion despite the new spend. The fund is meant as a war chest to insulate the economy from global volatility.
questions.source: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman proposed a USD 6.20 billion ‘Economic Stabilisation Fund’ last Friday, a war chest designed to insulate New Delhi from global volatility.

questions.prompt: While proposing an Economic Stabilisation Fund in March 2026, the Union government retained its FY26 fiscal deficit target at roughly what share of GDP under the revamped accounting system?
questions.explain: The FY26 fiscal deficit target of INR 15.58 trillion (USD 168 billion) works out to roughly 4.5% of GDP under the revamped accounting system. The government kept this target unchanged despite the new USD 6.20 billion fund.
questions.source: the government is sticking to its FY26 fiscal deficit target of INR 15.58 trillion (USD 168 billion), roughly 4.5% of GDP under the revamped accounting system.
